ruling_text: 2026-09-24 Jafar, in chat: THE WORKING BUSINESS DIRECTION, not a final one (production/research/runtime-ai-business, now on main). The game is sold once. Every copy includes an allowance of live conversation, counted on a server of ours. When a player uses it up, the street carries on with written lines and the in-character brush-off already ruled for a dropped connection. An optional mode lets players use their own AI key for unlimited talk, and later a mode lets capable cards run the talk themselves. The allowance's size is set once the slice has measured our real cost per hour, and it must comfortably exceed a normal playthrough, because for this game an allowance running out means the characters go quiet. The research's spreadsheet takes the measured cost per hour as its input when it exists. Two requirements into ROADMAP.md: every live AI call goes through a server of ours, the key never ships, model and provider swap on the server, the server counts each copy's allowance and has its own spending stop well below the provider's monthly cap (AI01-AI04); and the blind test of local line-writing is a priority, since writing lines is about 70 percent of the cost, still queued behind the slice's card measurement (L01). Onto the checklist before anyone outside his friends plays, whatever the final model: the AI notice, a way to report bad output, Steam's safeguards description, and the content rule enforced on everything said live (AI05-AI08).

Agreed with the builder: I made Darren's plain black leather lace-up boots, which failed their blind review against the bar (production/art/clothing/footwear/darren-boots-review-1.md: they hold in every pose but read as a placeholder; footwear lofted from the skin cannot reach the bar), so Epic's plainest boots go to the builder as a swap; he fits my ready pieces (Sheila's skirt, tights, handbag, spectacles; Darren's belt and pager; Ron's boots are in) and swaps Epic's plainest for Ron's jumper and trousers, Darren's jeans and boots, Sheila's cardigan and flats, and, since they failed against the bar on 1 October (production/art/clothing/sheila/ready-pieces-against-the-bar-2026-10-01.md), Sheila's blouse and Darren's T-shirt; the skirt passed.
summary: Principals' plain 1990 outfits: clothing's ready pieces fitted, Epic's plainest swapped in for the rest, judged against the bar.
